text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-Norway's pharmaceutical group Nycomed has decided to move its contrast agent production to Cork, Ireland. As a consequence 75 out of 120 Nycomed employees in Oslo will be made redundant.
-Only 50 percent of Norwegian companies paid tax in 1994, statistics from the Statistics Bureau show. The main reason is poor results in 1994 and earlier years.
- Unhappy with their salaries, 133 Norwegian NATO soldiers in former Yugoslavia have decided to go home. More soldiers are expected to return to Norway later.
-State owned wine importer Arcus will most probably be listed on the Oslo Bourse. The management suggest to privatise the company within the first six months of 1997.

-Norwegian pharmecutical group Nycomed will cut annual costs by 600 million crowns. In the short term the aim is to lessen the effect of the price fall in the American market, which will have full impact on earnings in the second half of 1996.
-Den norske Bank (DnB) posted rising profits in the first nine-months, but both Fokus Bank and Union Bank of Norway saw profits declining.
